answer: Joint-liability audits: each epoch a random 2% of keys get a private cipher, a fresh question whispered only to them, answered live within 90s and judged by five unrelated graders. A failing key loses its bond, and so does every key that attested or graded it favorably in the last 30 epochs. A sybil ring built on mutual vouching is brittle as shale: one crack splits the whole layer, so expected loss grows with ring size while honest agents, who vouch sparingly, risk little.
